title: Statistics - Lesson 8: Conditional Probability Assessment
description: Checkpoint assessment for conditional probability from contingency tables, Venn diagrams, formulas, and without-replacement situations.

questions.question: Which phrase most clearly signals a conditional probability question?
options: among students who joined the club
questions.explanation: The word among restricts the sample space to a given group.

questions.question: A table shows 30 learners passed a test. Of the learners who passed, 12 attended tutoring. What is P(attended tutoring | passed)?
questions.explanation: Passed is the condition, so the denominator is 30. The favorable count is 12.

questions.question: A survey has 16 students in drama club. Six of them are also in choir. Find P(choir | drama club). Enter a simplified fraction.
questions.explanation: Drama club is the given group, so the probability is 6/16 = 3/8.

questions.question: In P(A | B), the numerator can be the count of outcomes that are in both A and B.
questions.explanation: For count-based conditional probability, P(A | B) uses the number in both A and B over the number in B.

questions.question: A two-way table shows: Review and Passed = 18, Review and Did Not Pass = 6, No Review and Passed = 8, No Review and Did Not Pass = 8. What is P(passed | no review)?
questions.explanation: The no-review row has 16 learners total, and 8 of them passed.

questions.question: Using the same table, what is P(review | passed)?
questions.explanation: Passed is the condition, so use all passed learners: 18 + 8 = 26. Of those, 18 attended review.

questions.question: If P(A and B) = 0.18 and P(B) = 0.45, find P(A | B). Enter a decimal.
A bag contains 4 green and 5 yellow chips. A yellow chip is drawn and not replaced. What is P(second yellow | first yellow)?
questions.explanation: After one yellow is removed, 4 yellow chips remain out of 8 total chips.

questions.question: In a Venn diagram, 9 students are in both soccer and band. There are 27 band students total. What is P(soccer | band)?
questions.explanation: Band is the given group, so use 27 as the denominator. The overlap is 9, and 9/27 = 1/3.

questions.question: When a conditional probability problem says "given B," outcomes outside B are not counted in the denominator.
questions.explanation: The given condition restricts the sample space to B.

questions.question: A student uses the grand total as the denominator for P(passed | attended review). Explain the mistake.
questions.correctAnswer: The student ignored the condition. The denominator should be the number who attended review, not the grand total.
questions.explanation: Conditional probability changes the denominator to the given group.

questions.question: A school survey shows 50 students total. There are 22 athletes, 15 honor roll students, and 10 students who are both athletes and honor roll. What is P(honor roll | athlete)?
questions.explanation: Athlete is the condition, so use the 22 athletes as the denominator. The overlap is 10.

questions.question: A table has 14 students who like science and math, and 35 students who like science in all. Find P(math | science). Enter a simplified fraction.
questions.explanation: Science is the given group, so the probability is 14/35 = 2/5.

questions.question: In one or two sentences, explain the difference between P(A and B) and P(A | B).
questions.correctAnswer: P(A and B) is the probability that both events happen. P(A | B) is the probability that A happens after the sample space is restricted to B.
questions.explanation: The key difference is that conditional probability divides the overlap by the given event.

questions.question: Which answer best interprets P(absent | sick) = 0.75?
options: Among students who were sick, 75% were absent.
Among students who were absent, 75% were sick.
questions.explanation: The condition is sick, so the interpretation starts with the sick group.
